newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end slightly lower.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly lower in mixed and balanced trading on Wednesday and traders said the market had levelled off after rising for nearly a week.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): -0.03 pct to 105.05
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 to 103.95
Volume was a low 133 million shekels with most of the acivity concentrated in inflation-linked bonds.

"The market is very stable and it reached a new equilibrium. As long as interest rates remain unchanged and inflation expectations remain the same, the market will continue to move in a very tight range," said Miri Dagan at Clal Insurance.
"Yields on long CPI-linked bonds (now at 4.1 percent) will continue to move at 4.1 to 4.3 percent," she added.
Ronen Kaufman at Nesuah Trading and Investments said he believed that in the long run yields would fall towards 3.8 percent.
"In the short term, yields of four percent are a very strong psychological barrier, but the trend is clear and yields will eventually continue to decline falling below four percent," he said.
Dagan said unlinked bonds were stable after having made a big move since the beginning of the week.
"Unlinked bonds will also decline because the Bank of Israel must lower its key lending rate. It is clear that the economy is slowing and a rate cut is inevitable," Kaufman said.

Israel Discount Bank said in a report released on Tuesday that interest rates would fall by 0.5 percentage point during the second quarter due to a slowing economy but would hold steady in the third quarter.

Dollar-linked bonds continued going up as the U.S. currency continued to rise on overseas markets. In local trading the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3900 shekels against 3.3890 on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
